The foreman sends the same announcement again as a new message: still one flag.

Rev C is out, the crew confirms it, then announces work per Rev C.

An acknowledgement of a revision nobody contradicted and a question about the truck time.

limitations: Sample size is 22 synthetic cases written by the team, so the numbers show that the known paths work, not a rate on real site traffic.
Voice notes arrive as text here: speech to text is not part of this run.
Questions from crews and the wording of answers are not scored, only the flags.
Delivery to the real Telegram and email services is not tested: the channel modules run, and both send through their mocked service, so the formats are covered and the network is not.
One run per case at temperature 0; run-to-run variation of the model is not measured.

A repeated live run on the same commit missed the truck delivery case (p10-too-few-trucks) that this run passed, so the model is not perfectly repeatable and this is one measured result, not a guarantee. The committed recordings replay this run's answers.
The variants are written by the same model that reads them, so they share its habits; real site messages would be harder in other ways.
The variants keep the unit, sheet, revision, count and day of the original by construction; a real message that loses one of those is a different case, not covered here.
Voice notes, speech to text, channels and answers are not part of this run.
One run per case at temperature 0; run-to-run variation is not measured.

limitations: Six synthetic voice notes, one observation per level; this is not a field-accuracy estimate.
e34 and e53 already contain site noise at 8 and 5 dB. Added SNR is relative to each supplied recording.
Key scoring uses the published fixed-sample spelling/time rubric; unfamiliar paraphrases can fail it.
Same facts means identical fact type and data, excluding IDs, quotes, subjects and confidence. Semantic paraphrases of note data can fail it.

Baseline checks require stated unit/sheet/revision values and explicit clock hours in extracted facts. Other semantics and inferred calendar dates are not independently gold-labelled; same facts is stability, not gold accuracy.
A fact accepted from a transcription that loses a key is reported, never replaced or suppressed by this evaluator.
